apps.subtitle: A genre-first hierarchical music client for Plex
apps.localizedDescription:
Features:

• Album-Art focused - Browse by an album art grid instead of boring ol' text lists, and enjoy auto-extracted background and accent colours across the whole interface, making your entire music listening experience cohesive and aesthetic.
• Waveform Seeking - If you have Sonic Analysis enabled on your server, you already have all this wonderful data. Skip past the 6 minute ambient intro straight to the good stuff.
• Track popularity data - See the top tracks in an album based on crowdsourced popularity data supplied directly via Plex and obtained via users starring their own libraries, or see a unique popularity chart over an albums track listing to get the full picture.

versions.localizedDescription:
New Features:

• brand new "pulsar" visualiser. i spent loads of time and lots of music tweaking it to be super responsive and hypnotic to watch. I always loved visualisers, and i always loved the one that inspired this, and i think i've made it as good as it could be imo. give it a try!
• visualisers are now real time too. no more precompute. this means we've got em on iOS too. No android yet, sorry droiders. Soon maybe.
• a "clear screen" mode that just showcases the visualiser, good for a second monitor or casting to a tv. it also has an optional kind of karaoke sing-along type lyrics display if the song you're listening to has timed lyrics.
• cast to other plex players such as plexamp or anything else that can accept plex casting. This might be because i am working on an apple TV app, maybe.

Improvements:

• Discovery crates are supported on desktop now.
• background gradients are much smoother, no more banding at all as far as i can tell. even under worst possible case scenarios. just smooth all around.
• vastly reduced battery usage on ios (all) and gpu usage on macos 26.

Fixes:

• fixed a bug that was inflating local play counts (didnt touch your scrobbles or server play counts).
• fixed macOS title bar double click to maximise.

Available Binaries::

• macOS (Universal) - *_universal.dmg (works on Intel + Apple Silicon).
• Linux (x86_64) - *_amd64.AppImage / *_amd64.deb / *.x86_64.rpm.
• Linux (arm64) - *_aarch64.AppImage / *_arm64.deb / *.aarch64.rpm.
• Windows - *_x64-setup.exe (NSIS) or *_x64_en-US.msi (MSI).
• Android - .apk (sideload).
• iOS (iPhone) - *_ios-adhoc.ipa (sideload).

These builds are unsigned, so you'll get a warning the first time you open the app:

• macOS: right-click the app > Open, then if it tells you it's damaged (thanks MacOS), go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Scroll Down > Run Anyway. Or run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/ramus.app from your terminal to clear the quarantine flag.
• Windows: SmartScreen will show "Unknown publisher" - click "More info" > "Run anyway".
• Android: enable "Install unknown apps" for your file manager / browser, then tap the .apk.
• iOS (iPhone Only): sideload however you like, or use sidestore source https://1337raspberry.github.io/ramus.json to grab this automatically.

Feedback very welcome.
